overview: Nekoware v1's FastPlace is a byte-for-byte port of the Memeware 7.3 module: one @Handler-flagged Consumer on the lwjeb bus that writes mc.rightClickDelayTimer = 0 on every UpdateEvent. Vanilla's gate sets the timer to 4 at the top of rightClickMouse(), decrements it once per tick, and only fires the held-use branch while it reads exactly 0, so the module collapses the 4-tick action cooldown and lifts right-click placement from 5 actions per second toward the 20/s tick ceiling. The only differences from the Memeware original are the package name, the module display name ('FastPlace' without a space) and the Category.MISC registration line; the mechanism, the timing profile and the server-visible fingerprint (a denser C08 placement stream) are identical.

sections.p: The module is a constructor plus one public Consumer field. The constructor registers the module as 'FastPlace' under Category.MISC with key 0, and eventConsumer0 is marked with the lwjeb @Handler marker so the bus invokes its accept() on every UpdateEvent. The lambda body is a single assignment: mc.rightClickDelayTimer = 0. There are no settings, no onEnable/onDisable, no mode system and no other handlers, so the module has exactly one behavior and it is always on while toggled.

The same Minecraft.java touchpoints as the Memeware original apply in this fork: rightClickMouse() writes rightClickDelayTimer = 4 at line 1327, the run-tick loop decrements at lines 1453-1454, and the held-use branch at line 1791 requires the timer to be exactly 0 and the player not already using an item. The module's per-tick write lands between the decrement and the poll, so the cooldown never accumulates and each tick is eligible for a right-click action. The isUsingItem guard still prevents double-fire inside an active use animation, which means the gain is exactly the elimination of the 4-tick inter-action wait.

As with the Memeware parent, the observable effect is a placement-rate change, not a packet-content change: sustained right clicks collapse from one C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement every 200ms to one per tick (sub-50ms scatter at full CPS), and the same cadence applies to item use. Because the payloads are vanilla-faithful, the module is only detectable through timing statistics, which is what makes the placement-rate family of checks (NCP's FastPlace window, short-term tick counters) the relevant countering surface rather than any payload validation.

files.label: FastPlace.java (module logic)
files.explanation: The complete module: the constructor registers 'FastPlace' under Category.MISC, and the single @Handler-flagged Consumer field executes mc.rightClickDelayTimer = 0 on every UpdateEvent. Apart from the package name and the registration strings it is textually identical to me/memewaredevs/client/module/misc/FastPlace.java, which makes it a direct port rather than an independent implementation.

files.label: Minecraft.java (the timer being zeroed)
files.explanation: The three rightClickDelayTimer touchpoints of this fork: the write of 4 in rightClickMouse (line 1327), the per-tick decrement (lines 1453-1454) and the held-use gate at line 1791 that requires the timer to read exactly 0. The module's assignment defeats that gate by running between the decrement and the poll, so the field never carries a cooldown while the module is toggled.

countering.label: FastPlace (placement-rate window)
countering.explanation: NCP's blockplace FastPlace scores each real placement into an ActionFrequency(2, 1000) window (BlockPlaceData line 53) and a short-term tick counter: fullScore = fastPlaceBuckets.score(1f) against cc.fastPlaceLimit (default 15/s, DefaultConfig line 184), plus a fastPlaceShortTermLimit (6) placements in fastPlaceShortTermTicks (10) ticks (lines 59-89). Vanilla's 200ms cooldown keeps a legit player at 5 placements/s, far under both bounds, while this module's zeroed timer pushes sustained placement toward 20/s and exceeds the window limit, triggering the configured cancel actions from vl>5. Because the check only fires from the Bukkit BlockPlaceEvent path, the item-use C08s (facing 255, air position) that the same gate accelerates are never scored by it.

countering.label: Direction (facing validation)
countering.explanation: Direction extends AbstractBlockDirectionCheck and accumulates blockplace VL from the angular gap between the placement's claimed facing and the player's actual look direction, with a per-hit cooldown. The module sends honest facings, so standing-still fast place is invisible to it; its value is as the companion to the rate check, because a placement stream that chases a moving cursor (strafing placements) makes the look updates trail the placement packets and the sustained mismatch accumulates. A fixed-position placement spam defeats the direction check entirely, which is why the rate window remains the primary counter.

countering.label: BlockPlace packet listener (soup auto-heal only)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's BLOCK_PLACE packet adapter (lines 134-142) only inspects the held item and reacts when it is MUSHROOM_SOUP, feeding the AUTO_HEAL check; the tree contains no placement-rate, direction or placement-reach validation. The accelerated C08 stream from this module therefore passes Arc v2's block-place layer untouched, and any real pressure on Arc v2 comes from the movement layer (MorePackets max-packets 30/s, Flight) rather than from a placement check. This is a gap entry: the AC's block-place surface does not counter the module.
